comparisons.peer_topic: Non-U.S. Pension Plan Assets and Obligations
comparisons.peer_summary: As of November 3, 2024, non-U.S. pension plan assets totaled $229 million, with projected and accumulated benefit obligations of $260 million and $229 million, respectively.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose benefit obligations and plan assets specifically for their non-U.S. pension plans. For Broadcom, non-U.S. plan assets were $229 million with accumulated benefit obligations of $229 million and projected benefit obligations of $260 million, indicating the plan was underfunded on a projected basis. In contrast, Intel's non-U.S. plans had significantly larger accumulated benefit obligations of $1.7 billion. Furthermore, Intel explicitly states that only its non-U.S. plans had obligations in excess of plan assets for both 2024 and 2023, aligning with Broadcom's situation where projected obligations ($260 million) exceeded plan assets ($229 million).

sentences.text: As of December 28, 2024, the accumulated benefit obligations were $763 million and $1.7 billion for the US plan and non-US plans, respectively.
As of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, only non-US plans had projected benefit obligations and accumulated benefit obligations in excess of plan assets.
The fair value of pension plan assets as of November 3, 2024 and October 29, 2023 included $229 million and $204 million, respectively, of assets for our non-U.S. pension plans.
The projected benefit obligations as of November 3, 2024 and October 29, 2023 included $260 million and $202 million, respectively, of obligations related to our non-U.S. pension plans.
The accumulated benefit obligations as of November 3, 2024 and October 29, 2023 included $229 million and $188 million, respectively, of obligations related to our non-U.S. pension plans.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of August 29, 2024, the projected benefit obligations of the company's pension plans were $191 million with plan assets of $261 million, compared to $175 million in obligations and $232 million in assets as of August 31, 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Micron also discloses pension plan obligations and assets for its foreign sites. As of August 29, 2024, Micron's projected benefit obligations were $191 million against plan assets of $261 million, resulting in an overfunded status. This contrasts with Intel, which reported $1.7 billion in accumulated benefit obligations for non-U.S. plans and explicitly noted that these obligations exceeded plan assets. While both companies have non-U.S. pension obligations, Intel's non-U.S. plans are underfunded relative to obligations, whereas Micron's are overfunded.
